subject: MedSys: inference deployment & SLOs — post-demo recap & action items
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: MedSys demo follow-up — key pain points, SLOs, and next steps

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time to demo with us earlier today. Quick recap from my side while it's fresh, plus the immediate next steps we discussed.

Pain points you confirmed: 
- Latency spikes affecting clinician workflow during note generation (current P95 ~1.6s for 256-token prompts).
- High per-inference cost when batching is inefficient — main peak windows are 08:00–11:30 PST and 19:00–22:00 PST.
- Need for model auditability and retention controls for regulated data.

Goals we agreed on: 
1) Reduce P95 latency for 256-token generative completions to <=300ms for interactive use.
2) Achieve 3–4x throughput improvement during peak windows without sacrificing latency SLOs.
3) Ensure Private deployment option (VPC) with integration to your KMS and audit log export.

Technical notes from the call: 
- Target model family: open LLM (candidate: Llama-2 13B / Mistral-instruct / other 13–30B variants).
- Typical prompt sizes today: 120–450 tokens; target evaluation will include 256 and 1024 token profiles.
- Expected concurrency for PoC: 40 concurrent interactive users, average 2 requests/min per user (burst to 150 concurrent).

Attachments: MedSys-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan with dates) attached; I also sketched a simple topology we can iterate on.

Agreed next steps (action items):
- Redwood: provide a technical deep-dive document with recommended topology, expected latency/throughput SLOs, and a ballpark PoC cost estimate (deliverable by Mon, 2026-11-01).
- MedSys: share a 24-hour representative prompt set and anonymized throughput logs for 2 peak days.
- Schedule a 60–90 minute technical workshop with your infra/security team and our engineers (options: Nov 4 or Nov 6).

If any of the points above are off, tell me and I'll update the MAP. Otherwise, I'll follow up with the deep-dive and the proposed topology attachment on Monday.

Best,
Priyom Das

Hi Priyom —

This is great — thank you for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The P95 you quoted (1.6s) is our current prod baseline for the current LLM service we run. Our internal goal for clinician-facing flows is P95 <= 350ms for 256-token completions (we realize that depends on model choice).
- Concurrency estimate: the 40 concurrent users is accurate for the initial clinical team, but if the PoC is successful we'll need to scale to ~250 concurrent by Q1.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence is a hard requirement for production; for the PoC we can start with a document-level control set and an NDA.

Requested from us: I'll pull together the anonymized throughput logs (two peak days) and a sample prompt set and drop them in the Drive link by EOD Friday.

Timeline: Nov 4 works for the technical workshop for us — prefer morning (09:00–11:30 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive Monday.

Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: MedSys technical deep-dive (latency & throughput SLOs, topology options, PoC ask)

Hi Elena / Tom —

As promised, attached a short technical deep-dive and two topology options that map to the goals from our demo. Highlights below; full notes + attachments in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_medSys_PoC

Short TL;DR recommendations:
- PoC objective: validate interactive latency for clinician flows (256 tokens) and measure cost/throughput under peak burst.
- Target SLOs for PoC: P50 <= 80ms, P95 <= 320ms for 256-token completions; P95 <= 700ms for 1024-token completions (these assume optimized batching + KV cache).
- Baseline model candidate: Llama-2 13B (FP16) or Mistral-instruct 12B (FP16/quantized Q4). We recommend starting with the 13B family for predictable latency and lower memory needs.

Topology options (ballpark):
1) Private VPC (recommended for compliance):
  - 2 x A100-40GB (dedicated) as inference nodes behind a small autoscaler (scale to 4 nodes for bursts).
  - Prefix KV cache layer on dedicated memcached cluster (reduces repeated token costs ~30%).
  - Ingress routing policy: low-latency path to us-east-1 + automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant (quantized model) if scale > 4 nodes.
  - Expected steady-state throughput: ~20–25 qps (256-token) per A100; burst to ~80 qps across 4 nodes with batching and latency targets maintained.
  - Estimated PoC infrastructure hours: 2 A100s for 2 weeks + autoscale testing.

2) Redwood Dedicated (faster time-to-value):
  - Dedicated pool: 4 x NVIDIA A10G (shared within customer pool) with continuous batching on the runtime.
  - Expected steady-state throughput: ~12–16 qps (256-token) per A10G; better cost-efficiency for sustained workloads.
  - Latency: with appropriate batching caps, we can meet P95 <= 320ms for 256 tokens in most traffic shapes.

Operational notes specific to MedSys constraints: 
- Auditing: Redwood Private supports audit log export (syslog/S3) and KMS-integration for key control.
- Retention: we can configure token-level retention windows and automatic purge for PoC datasets.
- Data residency: recommend running in us-east region for minimal network egress; we can also run in us-west on request.

Ballpark PoC estimate (in attachments): PoC (2-week test) with Private VPC topology: ~$26k–$38k depending on whether you want dedicated A100s or use a reserved Dedicated pool. See medsys_poc_cost_estimate.xlsx for line-item details.

Requested deliverables from MedSys for PoC kickoff: 
- Anonymized 24-hour prompt set + two peak-day logs (Elena indicated these will be shared).
- Contact list for infra/security for the workshop (Nov 4 morning).
- Confirmation on whether SOC2 artifacts can be shared under an NDA for production evaluation.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Workshop: Nov 4, 09:00–10:30 PT — technical deep-dive and infra alignment (please confirm).
2) Sign PoC SOW and NDA (we can circulate drafts right after workshop).
3) Redwood to provision test environment and run baseline runs with your prompt set within 5 business days of receiving logs.

Attachments: medsys_topology_v1.png (PNG, 210KB); medsys_poc_cost_estimate.xlsx (XLSX, 52KB)

I'll let Marissa and David jump in on sizing and any additional infra asks.

Best,
